mechanism: web primary documentation read; paraphrases/inferences only, not archived page bodies

references.title: ReadFile
references.review_use: The synchronous count is initialized to zero before work. Anonymous closed-writer reads return false with broken-pipe error. A true zero-count pipe read may reflect a peer zero-byte write.

references.title: CreatePipe
references.review_use: Failed-call output parameters are indeterminate; callers may not assume their contents. Zero buffer size requests the system default, not a fixed kernel allocation.

references.title: Anonymous Pipe Operations
references.review_use: Anonymous pipes use a uniquely named pipe implementation; synchronous reads can return after peer writes and after all writers close.

references.title: WriteFile
references.review_use: Zero requested bytes is a null write whose behavior depends on the underlying communications technology.

references.title: CreateProcessW
references.review_use: Nonzero return signals success. PROCESS_INFORMATION receives new-process identification; this page does not promise valid ownership fields on a false return.

references.title: PROCESS_INFORMATION
references.review_use: The structure identifies a newly created process/thread; the documented handle-close obligation is explicitly described for successful creation.

references.title: CloseHandle
references.review_use: The input is a valid open-object handle. A numeric nonnull word is not such a proof.

references.title: HeapFree
references.review_use: Current documentation permits GetLastError after zero failure; no stale-native-error finding applies merely because candidate queries it.

references.title: HeapAlloc
references.review_use: Failure does not set the last error. Candidate correctly records allocation failure without a native code.
